headline: Double blow: Gas crisis and load shedding hit Dhaka residents
summary: Residents of Mohammadpur and other areas are struggling to cook as gas lines remain dry for weeks, and electric stoves are rendered useless by power cuts.
details: Residents of Mohammadpur's Chan Mia Housing have been without gas for nearly a month, with no clear timeline for when the supply will return.
Some residents reported that while they initially saw small amounts of gas for a few days, the connection has since been completely severed, causing extreme hardship.
To cope with the gas shortage, many households invested in electric stoves, but frequent load shedding has made this alternative ineffective.
One resident, Russel Das, shared that his food often gets ruined when the power goes out mid-cooking, adding a financial burden to his already limited income.
Affected citizens are demanding a clear schedule from Titas Gas and urging the government to take immediate action to resolve the crisis.
The crisis is not limited to Mohammadpur; severe gas shortages have also been reported in Kalabagan, Kafrul, Kazipara, West Tejturi Bazar, and Badda.
caption:
No gas for a month, and now the electricity is gone too. Dhaka residents are struggling just to cook a basic meal.

Residents of Mohammadpur's Chan Mia Housing have been without gas for nearly a month, with no clear timeline for when the supply will return.

Some residents reported that while they initially saw small amounts of gas for a few days, the connection has since been completely severed, causing extreme hardship.

To cope with the gas shortage, many households invested in electric stoves, but frequent load shedding has made this alternative ineffective.

One resident, Russel Das, shared that his food often gets ruined when the power goes out mid-cooking, adding a financial burden to his already limited income.

Affected citizens are demanding a clear schedule from Titas Gas and urging the government to take immediate action to resolve the crisis.

The crisis is not limited to Mohammadpur; severe gas shortages have also been reported in Kalabagan, Kafrul, Kazipara, West Tejturi Bazar, and Badda.

headline_marked: Supreme Court: [[Judicial Service members banned from coaching]]
headline: Supreme Court: Judicial Service members banned from coaching
summary: A new circular prohibits judges and judicial officers from engaging in commercial coaching activities, whether in-person or digital.
details: The Supreme Court of Bangladesh has issued a circular banning members of the Bangladesh Judicial Service from being involved with commercial coaching centers, both physical and digital.
The notification, signed by Registrar General Habibur Rahman Siddiqui of the High Court Division's judicial branch, was issued on Monday, August 24.
The directive aims to maintain professional discipline, neutrality, and the dignity of the judicial service, while ensuring public trust in the judiciary remains strong.
Under the new rules, members cannot be directly or indirectly involved in commercial coaching activities on any platform.
Judicial officers are also prohibited from allowing their names, designations, photos, or identities to be used for the promotion of such coaching centers.
Furthermore, they are barred from using or providing any confidential, unpublished, or official information obtained through their judicial duties for coaching purposes.
The circular also prohibits the preparation, editing, publication, or supply of educational materials for commercial coaching centers.
Any member of the service who violates these provisions will face appropriate disciplinary action according to applicable laws and regulations.
caption:
No more commercial coaching for judges. The Supreme Court has banned judicial officers from running or promoting coaching centers.

The Supreme Court of Bangladesh has issued a circular banning members of the Bangladesh Judicial Service from being involved with commercial coaching centers, both physical and digital.

The notification, signed by Registrar General Habibur Rahman Siddiqui of the High Court Division's judicial branch, was issued on Monday, August 24.

The directive aims to maintain professional discipline, neutrality, and the dignity of the judicial service, while ensuring public trust in the judiciary remains strong.

Under the new rules, members cannot be directly or indirectly involved in commercial coaching activities on any platform.

Judicial officers are also prohibited from allowing their names, designations, photos, or identities to be used for the promotion of such coaching centers.

Furthermore, they are barred from using or providing any confidential, unpublished, or official information obtained through their judicial duties for coaching purposes.

The circular also prohibits the preparation, editing, publication, or supply of educational materials for commercial coaching centers.

Any member of the service who violates these provisions will face appropriate disciplinary action according to applicable laws and regulations.
